clue.text: Showing lover I care, men go nuts

definitions.note: a showing is a film screening; someone who loves going to them

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the words before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone declares their devotion while the men around them go wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing lover' reads as a lover showing affection, but a showing is a screening at the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular filmgoer is a lover of showings, the screenings at a picture house.

clue.text: Appropriate, what finishes off John Does?

parts.note: 'what' points back at the punctuation mark printed just before it, a comma

indicators.note: the letter that finishes off the word John is its last one

parts.note: does are female deer

explanation.surface: A question about what puts an end to anonymous John Does, people of unknown identity.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own printed comma is part of the wordplay: 'what' refers to it, giving COMMA. John Doe is the US name for an unidentified man.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to seize it for your own use, as an army does with property.

clue.text: Gets to arch without point

parts.note: gets to means annoys or irritates, as needles does
arch as an adjective means knowing and cunning, like sly

explanation.surface: Something makes its way to an archway without any purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to no purpose is doing it pointlessly, unnecessarily.

clue.text: Fell over close to buffet car

indicators.note: the moor is laid over the letter, covering it on both sides

parts.note: a fell is an upland hill or moor in northern England

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here of buffet

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled over close to the buffet car on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb but is the noun: a stretch of high moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is an old-fashioned word for an automobile.

clue.text: Huge number try trademark climbs

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbs means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a logo is a company's trademark

explanation.surface: A huge number of attempts to register a trademark keeps rising.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for ten raised to the power of one hundred, an enormous figure.

clue.text: One hearing those people's current uprising is more crude

parts.note: an ear is the organ that hears

indicators.note: in a down clue, the current's letter rises to an earlier position in the word

parts.note: their means belonging to those people
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A listener notes that a group's current rebellion is cruder than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' moves the I of THEIR up one place, giving THIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse or vulgar, so the comparative means cruder.

clue.text: Horse's price and bet on it makes you sick

parts.note: SP is the starting price, a horse's odds at the start of a race
EW, each way, is a bet placed on a horse to win or be placed

explanation.surface: A punter finds that a horse's odds and his each-way stake turn his stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: SP and EW are British horse-racing betting terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick in the noun sense is vomit, which is what is thrown up.

clue.text: Fussy groom scratching bottom

indicators.note: scratching means striking out; in a down clue the bottom is the last letter

parts.note: to groom someone for a role is to prime or prepare them

explanation.surface: A fussy stable groom refuses to scratch his backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim describes someone stiffly proper and easily shocked, hence fussy.

clue.text: With time, you might make it as a worker

definitions.text: you might make it as a worker

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Given enough time, you might make a success of being an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make it' sounds like succeeding, but the definition means earn your pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is what an employee makes for labour, so a worker earns this.

clue.text: See 25
Chairman defends cycling holiday — he really knows his stuff!

indicators.note: the chairman's name surrounds and protects the other piece

parts.note: Chairman Mao, leader of Communist China

indicators.note: cycling sends the first letter of the word round to its end

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: A boss stands up for a cycling holiday as a true expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the R of REST to the end, giving ESTR.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso or master of an art is an expert who knows their field thoroughly.

clue.text: Biggest bouncer is ripping you off

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, bounds along
king-sized means the biggest, so king describes the largest

explanation.surface: The heftiest nightclub doorman is fleecing you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman; it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle or cheat them, slang for overcharging.

clue.text: Risky option, spread on a roll's soft spot

indicators.note: spread out means the letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: to have a thing for someone is to have a soft spot for them

explanation.surface: A gamble with butter spread on the soft part of a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice that wins everything or loses everything is a gamble with no middle ground.

clue.text: Gracious when, at first, young swimmer's keeping score

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of when
keeping means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an elver is a young eel; the 's stands for has
to score is to scratch a line

explanation.surface: A child swimming in a race keeps count of points, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, as in 'Goodness gracious!'

clue.text: Why person I capture holds fast

indicators.note: the words before it hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a person they captured is held fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like part of 'holds fast', meaning firmly; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic speeds above five times that of sound are extremely fast.

clue.text: Treat sea water and supply deltas

indicators.note: read as 'in a supple way', so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Purifying sea water and piping it to river deltas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like providing, but it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing salt from seawater makes it drinkable, a desalination process.

clue.text: Sport LAX badge at terminal

parts.note: LAX read as LA followed by X, a cross

indicators.note: the terminal of a word is its last letter, here of badge

explanation.surface: A sports badge is shown at the terminal of Los Angeles airport, LAX.
explanation.walkthrough: LAX is also American slang for this sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A field game played with netted sticks, originally North American.

clue.text: Works on best clothes

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a memo
finery is one's best clothing

explanation.surface: Someone toils away in their smartest outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a verb but is a noun, an industrial plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that purifies oil or sugar is an industrial site, a works.

clue.text: Condition of drunk at bedside, taking off drag

indicators.note: drunk means the letters have been knocked about into a new order

parts.note: D stands for drag in aerodynamics, where lift is L and drag is D

explanation.surface: A drunk at someone's bedside takes off women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' suggests cross-dressing; it supplies the D removed from the letters of AT BEDSIDE before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medical condition of high blood sugar, so it is an example of a condition.

clue.text: Fan of diversity to vote for one conservative over another

indicators.note: the voting word is laid over the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to elect is to vote for
I is the Roman numeral for one
another conservative, so another C

explanation.surface: A lover of variety votes for one Tory candidate in preference to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with broad tastes who draws on many sources welcomes variety.

clue.text: Donk pushed girl with Tristan

parts.note: Donk is the setter, who speaks of himself as I
a drug dealer pushes drugs, so pushed means sold, and the drug sold is E, ecstasy

explanation.surface: The setter shoved a young woman who was with Tristan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushed' in the drug-dealing sense gives SOLD plus E, the slang for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan and Isolde are the doomed lovers of Arthurian legend and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Kit for PC essentially skewered opening of bookies (somewhere to punt)

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central part, its middle letters
the opening of bookies is its first letter

parts.note: the Cam is the river at Cambridge, famous for punting

explanation.surface: A computer user was skewered at the bookmakers' over a place to bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a bet at the bookies; it is the flat boat poled along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A small camera attached to a computer is a piece of kit for it.

clue.text: Maybe makes Oxford qualities surface

parts.note: an Oxford is one kind of shoe, and a cobbler makes shoes
tones are qualities of sound or colour

explanation.surface: Something perhaps gives the city of Oxford its distinctive character on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the university city, but it is a lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounded stones set in a street make a paved surface.

clue.text: On the tours of Trinity

indicators.note: tours means goes round, so the word the encircles the other piece

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Visitors are taken on guided tours of Trinity College.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trinity' looks like the college; it is a set of a certain number.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinity is a group of a set size, so it stands for that number.

clue.text: Bob's face (having pleasured himself?)

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: Bob's expression after a solitary act of self-gratification.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling, the old British coin, written s. The definition's question mark flags the pun on self-satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pleased with oneself is self-satisfaction, the sense played on as self-pleasure.

clue.text: He comes out in rash just outside London

indicators.note: rash means reckless, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man breaks out in a skin rash on the edge of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin condition, but it is the adjective, hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: This names the counties that surround London, so they lie just beyond the capital.

clue.text: When one can no longer see satellite show behind schedule

definitions.text: When one can no longer see satellite

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare behind
to set a date is to schedule it

explanation.surface: A broadcast of a satellite is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind schedule' looks like a phrase meaning late; it splits between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment our natural satellite dips below the horizon, it can't be seen.

clue.text: Traders shifting mascara vandalise boxes

indicators.note: boxes means holds within, so the letters sit inside those words

explanation.surface: Merchants moving cosmetics damage the packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: A company of merchants travelling together across a desert is a moving band.

clue.text: Joy to get going about 50

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: gee up is a call to get a horse going
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The delight of getting started at around fifty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight and high spirits are synonyms of happiness.

clue.text: Not reflecting my scream, it's fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic means wild and fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mirror fails to show my scream, which is extraordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking symmetry, the two halves are not mirror images of each other.
